blogs.title: "Beyond Chest Pain – Hidden Abdominal Injuries Can Hijack Lung Symptoms"
blogs.description: This post explores how massive unilateral blood‑stained effusions may stem from deep pancreatic injury rather than classic pulmonary disease when prior blunt abdominal trauma is overlooked. Using our child’s case narrative it highlights key bedside clues prompting physicians to revisit trauma history early—circumstances where missed injury prompts empirical tuberculosis treatment instead of targeted investigation.

blogs.title: "Peering Through Amylases – Why Hyperamylasemia Berserk Blood‑Stained Effusions”
blogs.description: Here we dive deep into why markedly elevated pleural amylases (>1000 U/L) herald pancreatic leakage and how serum/pleura enzyme typing differentiates pancreatic type from salivary type—a crucial checkpoint ruling out empyema or malignancy early.

blogs.title: "Imaging Mindset – Choosing CT, MRCP and ERCP When Lungs Mask Pancreases"
blogs.description: "Pleura leak matters under diaphragm," we explain variable sensitivities between CT (limited fistula depiction), MRCP (70–80%% sensitivity), and ERCP (gold standard therapeutic view). Practical guidance covers what images chase first once hyperamylasemia surfaces.

blogs.title: "Conservative Care First – Managing Pediatric PPF With NPO, TPN and Octreotide"
blogs.description: "Surgery waits," stresses this vignette showing that nil‑per‑oral feeding plus somatostatin analogues consistently halts fistular drainage even before stenting becomes necessary—a realistic algorithm reflecting current literature success rates.

blogs.title: "Hereditary Underpinnings – Why Genetics Matters in Paediatric Pancreatitis Complications"
blogs.description:
__Genetic testing becomes paramount__when chronic pancreatitis presents early or recurs unpredictably—as noted in SPINK1 / PRSS1 mutations seen worldwide—and often precipitates rare sequelae such as PPF post‑trauma.

 We discuss indications for panel workup, family counselling integration.

 Highlights prevention cues including surveillance schedules for high-risk children.
